trace.final_message:
`hourglass/gaps.py` now has `find_gaps(worked, hours)`, and it is committed as c221a27. The full suite passes with 34 tests, 8 of them new, and `make lint` is clean.

- **Behavior:** it merges the worked spans, so overlapping or touching spans leave no gap. It returns one label per uncovered stretch, such as `gap 12:00-13:00 (60 min)`. If nobody worked, it returns a single label for all of opening hours. Input order does not matter.
- **Exception:** a worked span that starts before opening or ends after closing raises `ValueError`. The message names the offending span.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_gaps.py` covers a gap in the middle, full coverage, touching and overlapping spans, gaps at both ends, nobody working, unordered input, and both out-of-hours cases.
- **Extras you did not ask for:** I added a line to `docs/api.txt` and an entry under Unreleased in `CHANGES.txt`.
- **Not done:** I did not export `find_gaps` from `hourglass/__init__.py`. Callers import it from `hourglass.gaps`.
- **Project notes:** the style rules in `CLAUDE.md` pushed the file away from usual Python style in a few places. There is one blank line between functions instead of two. Imports are in reverse alphabetical order, and `_uncovered` has no return annotation so its signature fits in 60 characters. The whole file was also kept to 60-character lines and 8-line functions.
- **Review:** I reviewed `git diff` before committing.

before.docs/api.txt:
hourglass.parsing.parse_clock(text): read a clock time as minutes since midnight
hourglass.parsing.format_clock(minutes): minutes since midnight as HH:MM
hourglass.parsing.parse_span(text): read a range such as 09:00-17:30
hourglass.parsing.format_span(span): a span as start-end text
hourglass.parsing.normalize_day(text): short lowercase day name
hourglass.merging.spans_overlap(first, second): whether two spans share any time
hourglass.merging.intersect_spans(first, second): the part two spans share
hourglass.merging.merge_spans(spans): collapse overlaps into a sorted list
hourglass.merging.total_minutes(spans): minutes covered, overlaps counted once
hourglass.schedule.parse_schedule_text(text): parse schedule CSV held in memory
hourglass.schedule.load_schedule(path): read a schedule CSV from disk
hourglass.schedule.shifts_for_worker(shifts, worker): all shifts for one worker
hourglass.schedule.worker_minutes(shifts): scheduled minutes per worker
hourglass.schedule.day_coverage(shifts, day): merged spans for a day
hourglass.schedule.format_day_line(shifts, day): one text line for a day
